title: If You Own Silver or Gold, Please Don't Make This Mistake
speaker: Jordan Roy-Byrne

macro_themes.view: Gold and silver are in secular bull markets; buy, hold and trim, and don't trade in and out.
The precious metals correction does not have much longer or deeper to go; most damage is done.
A peak and roll-over in the 2-year yield (near 5%) would mark the end of the drawdown and start the next leg up for gold.
Implied allocation to precious metals (3.7%) and gold (~1.9%) is tiny vs past peaks, so this is not 1980 or 2011.
S&P/gold ratio may rally another 6-8% to its falling 40/80-month averages, then roll over as capital rotates from stocks to metals.

calls.reason: Broke out of a 13-year cup and handle; down 29%, maybe a bit more, but no 40-50% correction; next leg up when 2-year yield rolls over.
calls.quote: we're not going to see a 50% or 40% correction right now. So, you shouldn't be worried about that much more downside

calls.reason: Broke out of a 45-year base; down 55%, similar to 2008 decline; strong support at 48-50.
calls.quote: when we're looking out the next 5 or 10 years, this is going to be trading in the hundreds of dollars per ounce

calls.reason: Breadth above 200-day not yet washed out; GDXJ could fall another 10-13% to strong support near 94, then a major bottom and big move up.
calls.quote: GDXJ could still decline here 10, 12, 13% or so down to this really strong support

notes: No date spoken; end-of-week video ("as this week closes", "great weekend ahead"), date from listing. Silver "hundreds of dollars" over 5-10 years not given as a number, so no target. GDXJ normalised to GDX ticker, levels in GDXJ units; short-term he noted a rebound first, so the 94 downside is more weeks out.
